stepAnswer: integral from 0 to 2 of (4-x^2) dx + integral from 2 to 3 of (x^2-4) dx
stepBody: The curve $f(x) = x^2 - 4$ crosses the x-axis. To find the total area between the curve and the x-axis from $x = 0$ to $x = 3$, we need to account for regions above and below the axis.\n\nFirst, find where $f(x) = 0$, then describe how to set up the integral for the total area.
